# Run NuRec Reconstruction

**Source execution:** Read `$NUREC_WORKDIR/nurec-runtime.md`, generated by
`run.sh`, before executing commands. For every root-workspace `bazel` command
below, use its literal Docker/Bazel prefix with the same target and arguments.
Only the standalone converter workspace runs Bazel on the host. Do not extract
release archives into host caches or invent module overrides.

This is the operating specification for an autonomous step that runs NuRec reconstruction
on validated NCore V4 data. The agent generates auxiliary data, selects or creates a config,
runs reconstruction, and produces a structured diagnosis if issues are detected.

---

## 1. Input Schema

```yaml
# Required
ncore:
  converter_dir: <string> # Path to the NCore converter repo
data:
  ncore_path: <string> # Path to validated NCore V4 sequence_meta.json
  description: <string> # High-level dataset overview (carried from build-ncore-converter)
  profile: <mapping> # Optional structured dataset facts from audit-dataset

nurec:
  camera_ids: [<string>, ...] # Optional reconstruction camera scope.
  lidar_ids: [<string>] # Exactly one LiDAR for now.
  output_dir: <string|null> # Default: <ncore.converter_dir>-nurec-out
  dev_deps_image: <string|null> # Optional; defaults to the checkout's build-image pin.
  source_dir: <string|null> # Optional; defaults to the enclosing checkout.

# When present, apply `nurec.camera_ids` and `nurec.lidar_ids` to the NuRec
# launch and fail fast if any listed sensor is absent from the shard.
```

The launcher resolves the source and matching image into `$NUREC_WORKDIR/nurec-runtime.md`. Use that pair for validation, auxiliary generation, and reconstruction. Also use any additional read-only build mounts recorded there: development-checkout authentication and linked-worktree metadata when needed.

---

## 2. Instructions

> **Step attempt entry anchor:** capture `runs[*].started_at` here, before the first action under "Pre-flight checks"; see [nurec-onboard/SKILL.md "Timestamp capture rules"](../../SKILL.md#timestamp-capture-rules) for the step-attempt definition.

### Python / NCore execution rule

Any Python helper or snippet in this step that imports `ncore` MUST run under the converter's Bazel environment, not with system `python3`. Add a small converter-local Bazel target or extend an existing Bazel-run script for ad-hoc probes; do not run `python3 -c`, `python3 script.py`, or a standalone notebook cell for NCore API access.

### Pre-flight checks

1. Parse input with `lib/parse_input.py`; resolve these values from grouped input keys:

   - `$ncore_converter_dir` from `ncore.converter_dir`, bound as a shell variable.
   - `$nurec_output_dir` from `nurec.output_dir`, bound as a shell variable, defaulting to `<ncore.converter_dir>-nurec-out`.
   - `<dev_image>` and `<nurec_src>` from `$NUREC_WORKDIR/nurec-runtime.md`, validated by the launcher against the checkout's build-image pin.
   - `<build_mounts>` from that file: the literal additional mounts; omit this line when that file says none.
   - `<workdir>`, the absolute `NUREC_WORKDIR`; `<nurec_cache>` is `<workdir>/nurec-bazel`.
   - `<username>`, the host username from `id -un`.
   - `<run_name>`, the basename of `$NUREC_WORKDIR` with every character outside
     `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` replaced by `-`. It makes the container names below unique per
     workdir, so containers left by runs in other workdirs never block a launch.

   The image and run names are written as `<placeholders>` because they appear only in
   `docker` commands, where the resolved text has to be substituted in literally
   (see
   [docker-execution.md "One command, literal arguments"](docker-execution.md#one-command-literal-arguments)).

2. `run.sh` pulls the matching dev dependencies image, builds the development
   image on it, probes the GPU inside the development image, and prepares
   writable build-home/ccache directories and `<nurec_cache>/nurec.bazelrc`.
   The development image provides the build tooling and dependencies; the
   commands below build and run the enclosing checkout with Bazel.
   If Docker's default bridge cannot reach build dependencies or model weights,
   add `--network host` to the aux-generation and reconstruction commands. See
   [docker-execution.md "Network egress check"](docker-execution.md#network-egress-check).

3. Verify the sequence meta JSON parses as V4 (`version`, `sequence_id`, `sequence_timestamp_interval_us`, `component_stores`) and every component-store path ends in `.zarr.itar`. Directory-format stores (`.zarr/`) fail NuRec with a misleading `AssertionError: provided path ... not a file` on the JSON, not the store; re-run the converter with `--store-type itar`.
4. **Resolve `selected_lidar_id`** so auxiliary-data generation and NuRec training
   consume the same LiDAR. Apply the LiDAR-selection policy from config selection here once,
   up front:

   - When `nurec.lidar_ids` is present, require exactly one
     entry for now, set `selected_lidar_id` to that value, verify it appears in
     the sequence meta JSON's `component_stores`, and record
     `operator_override: true` for the diagnosis `nurec_lidar_selection` entry.
   - Otherwise, enumerate `lidar_ids_all` from the meta JSON and apply the policy
     in [LiDAR selection for reconstruction](#lidar-selection-for-reconstruction): prefer the
     longest-range, widest-FOV unit (typically a roof-mounted 360-deg spinning
     LiDAR); exclude short-range side / corner units. Set `selected_lidar_id` to
     the chosen id and record `operator_override: false`.

   The LiDAR-selection prose remains the source of truth for the policy
   itself; this step just makes the resolved id available to the aux-generation
   command. Without it, auxiliary-data generation processes for every LiDAR (wasted compute on
   multi-LiDAR shards) or for a non-deterministic subset, and NuRec training may consume
   aux that doesn't match the trained LiDAR.

### Generate auxiliary data

> **Docker execution rules apply to every `docker run` below** (one command with
> literal arguments, flag rules, `--user <uid>:<gid>`, and the detach + per-call
> polling pattern for long-running containers). See
> [docker-execution.md](docker-execution.md) before running any aux-generation or
> reconstruction container.

If `<workdir>`, `<data_dir>` or `<nurec_output_dir>` resolve to the same path, include that writable mount only once in the commands below. Docker rejects duplicate mount destinations.

NuRec requires auxiliary data (semantic segmentation, LiDAR segmentation, etc.) generated by `//apps:nurec_tools -- ncore-aux-data`:

```bash
docker run --shm-size=64g --gpus all -d \
  --name nurec-tools-<sequence_id>-<run_name> \
  --user <uid>:<gid> \
  -e HOME=<nurec_cache>/build-home -e USER=<username> \
  -e CCACHE_DIR=<nurec_cache>/ccache -e HF_TOKEN \
  <build_mounts> \
  -v <nurec_src>:<nurec_src>:ro \
  -v <workdir>:<workdir> \
  -v <data_dir>:<data_dir> \
  -w <nurec_src> \
  <dev_image> \
  bazelisk --output_base=<nurec_cache>/output_base --bazelrc=<nurec_cache>/nurec.bazelrc \
  run //apps:nurec_tools -- ncore-aux-data \
  --dataset-path=<data_dir>/<sequence_meta.json> \
  --output-dir=<data_dir> \
  --camera-id=<cam1> --camera-id=<cam2> \
  --lidar-id=<selected_lidar_id> \
  --store-meta \
  --no-seg-logits \
  --lidar-seg-camvis
```

Point `<data_dir>` at the directory containing `.zarr.itar` + `.json`, and send aux output there too so NuRec finds it alongside the sequence JSON. Pass the **sequence meta JSON** via `--dataset-path`. `--camera-id` can be repeated; omit to process every camera. Camera IDs come from the sequence meta JSON. **`--lidar-id` must match the `selected_lidar_id` resolved during pre-flight** (NuRec training uses a single LiDAR; aux generated for any other LiDAR is wasted compute and goes unused). On single-LiDAR shards the flag can be omitted -- `ncore-aux-data` defaults to every shard LiDAR -- but passing it explicitly keeps auxiliary-data generation and NuRec training in lockstep. `--num-threads <N>` speeds up processing. `--store-meta` records the invocation's own provenance; it does **not** register the generated aux stores in the sequence meta, so NuRec discovers aux purely by filename next to the sequence JSON (see [build-ncore-converter/conventions.md "Sequence ID constraints"](../build-ncore-converter/conventions.md#sequence-id-constraints)).

**Verify aux ITAR integrity after the tools container exits** (each `.aux.*.zarr.itar` must end with `b'itar'` at offset -512; a missing magic means the container crashed before finalizing the index block):

```bash
python3 -c "
import glob, sys
bad = []
for p in glob.glob('<data_dir>/*.aux.*.zarr.itar'):
    with open(p, 'rb') as f:
        f.seek(-512, 2)
        if f.read(4) == b'itar':
            continue
        bad.append(p)
if bad: print('CORRUPT aux ITARs:', bad); sys.exit(1)
print('All aux ITARs OK')
"
```

If corrupt, re-run with `--no-lidar-seg-camvis` to skip LiDAR segmentation (the most common crash site).

**If the tools container exits immediately with an `AssertionError` matching `CuboidsComponent.*not found`** (visible via `docker logs` -- the literal observed wording is `AssertionError: CuboidsComponent group 'default' not found`, raised in NCore's `ncore/impl/data/v4/compat.py`): the NCore shard is missing a `CuboidsComponent`. `ncore-aux-data` requires it unconditionally, even with `--no-lidar-seg-camvis`. Match the regex `AssertionError.*CuboidsComponent.*not found` rather than the exact string so a future quote-style or wording drift in NCore does not break routing. Route as a `ncore_data_issue` back to `build-ncore-converter`:

- symptom: `"ncore-aux-data crashes with AssertionError matching CuboidsComponent.*not found"`
- likely_cause: `"converter does not write CuboidsComponent when dataset has no cuboid annotations"`
- suggested_fix: `"add empty CuboidsComponent write in _write_cuboids (zero observations)"`

**Auxiliary data flags** (`ncore-aux-data` options, default shown):

| Data                   | Flag                                           | Default       |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Semantic segmentation  | `--segmentation-backend`                       | `mask2former` |
| LiDAR seg + visibility | `--lidar-seg-camvis` / `--no-lidar-seg-camvis` | enabled       |
| Depth estimation       | `--depth-backend`                              | `none`        |
| DINOv2 features        | `--dinov2-backend`                             | `none`        |
| Ego mask estimation    | `--ego-mask` / `--no-ego-mask`                 | disabled      |
| Ego mask sampling rate | `--ego-mask-samples-per-second`                | 0.2           |

**Ego mask decision rule.** Before running the tools container, check whether the shard contains a `MasksComponent` by probing the sequence meta JSON:

```python
import json, math
meta = json.load(open("<data.ncore_path>"))
# The sequence meta JSON records which component groups exist; mask_names per
# camera are stored inside the zarr .zattrs and are not visible here. Presence
# of a "masks" component group is sufficient signal that the converter wrote
# ego masks -- inspect the zarr if you need per-camera key confirmation.
has_masks_component = any(
    isinstance(store, dict)
    and isinstance(store.get("components"), dict)
    and "masks" in store["components"]
    for store in meta.get("component_stores", [])
)
```

- `has_masks_component == True` → add `--ego-mask` **and** set `--ego-mask-samples-per-second` explicitly (see [Generate auxiliary data](#generate-auxiliary-data)'s ego-mask sampling-rate rule). NuRec loads the static `"ego"` key from the shard's `MasksComponent` as its primary ego signal; the `ncore-aux-data` aux egomask is an independent artifact used for Cosmos packaging and cross-checking.
- `has_masks_component == False` → `--ego-mask` is still beneficial (the aux computation becomes the only ego signal). Accuracy depends on the quality of automatic ego-vehicle segmentation from that camera's perspective.

**Ego mask sampling rate.** When `--ego-mask` is enabled, set the rate high enough that the `majority` aggregation sees enough samples to produce a stable result. With 1 sample no aggregation occurs at all; genuine majority requires at least 3. Use 5 as a safe working minimum. Compute the rate:

```python
duration_sec = (meta["sequence_timestamp_interval_us"]["stop"] -
                meta["sequence_timestamp_interval_us"]["start"]) / 1e6
samples_per_second = max(1.0, math.ceil(5 / duration_sec))
```

Use at least `1.0` regardless of duration. At the default `0.2` samples/sec a 5-second sequence yields only 1 sample — no aggregation occurs, just a single-frame estimate sensitive to that one frame's content. Setting the rate via the formula above ensures robust majority voting while keeping compute proportional to sequence length.

### Select or create app config

**Dynamic vs static decision rule (required).** Probe the shard for potentially-dynamic cuboids first; a dynamic config variant is mandatory when any are present (static configs do not reconstruct moving objects -- they only use cuboids to mask dynamic regions). Use an **exclusion list of known-static classes** rather than a dynamic allow-list -- NCore `class_id` is a free-form string and the vocabulary is source-dependent, so any unrecognized class is treated as potentially dynamic:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from ncore.impl.data.v4.components import SequenceComponentGroupsReader, CuboidsComponent

# Known-static classes; everything else is treated as potentially dynamic.
# Class-name vocabularies are source-dependent, so extend this set per dataset
# rather than maintaining a dynamic allow-list (which would silently misclassify
# any unfamiliar class).
STATIC_ONLY_CLASSES = {"barrier", "billboard", "cone", "guardrail", "lamp_post", "pole", "sign", "traffic light", "traffic sign", "traffic_cone", "traffic_light", "traffic_sign"}

reader = SequenceComponentGroupsReader([Path("<data.ncore_path>")])
has_dynamic_cuboids, observed_classes = False, set()
for rd in reader.open_component_readers(CuboidsComponent.Reader).values():
    for obs in rd.get_observations():
        observed_classes.add(obs.class_id)
        if obs.class_id.lower() not in STATIC_ONLY_CLASSES:
            has_dynamic_cuboids = True
# Full scan completes so observed_classes contains every class_id in the shard.
# Log observed_classes in the step summary and use it to list dynamic classes
# in the fail-fast message when has_dynamic_cuboids is True.
```

`has_dynamic_cuboids == True` requires a dynamic-family config (bundled name matches `*_dynamic*.yaml`, or the config resolves `/model: gaussians/composite/dynamic_gaussians`). If the shard has dynamic cuboids and the authored config is static, **fail fast** before launching reconstruction and list the observed classes.

**Directional-quality SQA recipe (always-author).** NuRec Onboard always writes a custom config -- never points `--config-name` at a bundled `apps/AV/...` directly -- because every bundled config bakes in dataset-specific sensor IDs (e.g. `camera_front_wide_120fov`, `lidar_gt_top_p128_v4p5`) that mismatch the shard at launch time. The custom config composes NuRec's published "sanity-quality assessment" recipe (`apps/prod/<dataset>/sqa_default.yaml` family in the NuRec repo): it inherits a base 3DGUT config, layers the prod options that disable expensive optional artifact pipelines, and pins the shard's actual sensors. NuRec ships this recipe as the directional-quality default; it produces a usable reconstruction in ~3-4× less wall time than the full-quality variant by pixel-subsampling the camera loss and skipping the optional artifact exports. The authored config takes the artifact-export skips but trains at full resolution: this workflow judges whether a converter produced a faithful shard, and subsampled supervision softens high-frequency detail in a way that reads as a conversion defect.

**Justify every field the authored config sets.** Reading a bundled `apps/AV/...` config to source a specific fact is legitimate, and the steps below call for it. Copying a field is a separate act that needs its own reason: a bundled dataset config is an internally consistent package whose fields are tuned against each other, including that file's own sensor selection and subsampling, so a value lifted out of one arrives in the authored config without the context that made it correct. Copy the fact the step asks for and leave every field the step does not ask for at its inherited default. Any field the authored config sets beyond the skeleton below carries a comment giving its reason, so the operator reading the config can tell a deliberate setting from one that rode along with a copy.

**Match validation-video playback FPS to input camera cadence.** NuRec's validation MP4 writer uses the scalar `system.test.video_fps` when encoding `val/pred_*.mp4`. Set it in the authored custom config so validation videos play back at the same cadence as the input camera data rather than inheriting a bundled dataset default.

Compute the input camera cadence from the NCore camera timestamps for the cameras that the config will use (operator-provided list when present, otherwise the enumerated shard cameras).

Use the median adjacent frame-end delta per camera, then the median across cameras. NCore camera timestamps are in microseconds, so `1_000_000 / delta_us` converts the median inter-frame interval to frames per second (`1_000_000 us/sec / 100_000 us = 10 fps`):

```text
input_camera_fps_hz = median(1_000_000 / median_adjacent_frame_end_delta_us(camera))
val_video_fps = round(input_camera_fps_hz / dataset.val_camera_frame_step)
```

Cross-check the cadence against the input time window before authoring the config. When `duration_sec` is present, each selected camera should have roughly `duration_sec * input_camera_fps_hz` frames before `dataset.val_camera_frame_step` sampling; allow a small tolerance for inclusive/exclusive window boundaries and dropped frames. Also compare the median-delta estimate above with the full-span estimate `(num_camera_frames - 1) / ((last_frame_end_us - first_frame_end_us) / 1_000_000)`. A large disagreement means the timestamp probe, selected camera list, or input time window is wrong and must be resolved before setting `system.test.video_fps`.

Use `val_video_fps` for `system.test.video_fps`. The field is an integer; if a dataset has a non-integer cadence (for example 29.97 Hz), round to the nearest integer. If cameras have mixed cadences, use the median across the cameras included in the run.

**Enable the quality metrics this workflow reports.** `system.test.metrics.ssim.enabled` and `system.test.metrics.lpips.enabled` are false in the inherited defaults, and neither the base 3DGUT config nor any of the prod option blocks the skeleton layers on top sets them, so a config that does not name them reports PSNR and nothing else. [config-skeleton.yaml](config-skeleton.yaml) enables both, because the diagnosis interprets all three (see [diagnosis-reference.md](diagnosis-reference.md)) and the workflow summary requires all three at `workflow_status: success`. LPIPS fetches its backbone weights on the first validation pass, so on a host whose default bridge network cannot reach the weight CDN the run fails at validation rather than at startup -- the [network egress check](docker-execution.md#network-egress-check) determines whether this host needs `--network host`.

Leave `system.test.metrics.cpsnr` alone. It is enabled by default but computes only where a camera carries semantic labels, and it reports per-class values rather than one scalar, so on a shard without semantic segmentation it contributes nothing to `metrics.yaml` either way.

Write the skeleton out with every `FILL IN` marker resolved from the shard, and mount it for the NuRec launch. The placeholder each marker replaces overrides the inherited default and then cannot be used, so one left unsubstituted fails when NuRec reaches it rather than running under a plausible default.

Why each prod option matters:

- **Full image resolution (default).** Three knobs control it and NuRec expects them to agree: `dataset.samplers.batch_sampler.camera_pixel_sampler.subsample`, `dataset.n_val_image_subsample`, and `dataset.n_train_sequential_image_subsample`. The skeleton sets all three to `1`, so training, validation, and train-sequential decoding all run at the shard's native resolution. Subsampling is the dominant wall-clock lever in the other direction -- factor 4 is roughly a 3-4× per-step speedup -- so a long sequence or a wide camera set can be worth trading down. Opt in by layering `/apps/prod/options/subsampling/3dgut: batch_sampler_2` (or `batch_sampler_4`) and setting all three fields to that factor. NuRec ships no `batch_sampler_1`, which is why factor 1 is written as field values rather than selected as a block, and the option block alone covers only the training sampler: without the two `dataset` fields, validation and train-sequential decoding stay at the `/dataset: ncore` default of 4.
  - **Image-dimension constraint.** Factor `N` requires every camera image's H and W to be divisible by `N`; the pixel sampler tiles the image into NxN super-pixels and assumes a whole-tile partition. With non-divisible dimensions training fails at startup before the first optimizer step. Factor 1 divides every dimension, so this binds only on a run that opted into 2 or 4; the lowest-friction fix there is to step the factor down until it divides H and W cleanly across every camera in the shard, since padding or cropping at converter time costs a converter re-run.
- **Pre-launch subsampling check (required).** Before launching the NuRec training container, resolve the selected camera list and inspect one image shape for each selected camera from the validated NCore shard. Confirm that all three knobs above hold the same factor and that the factor divides every selected width and height. At the default factor of 1 both conditions hold by construction, and the check is a cheap guard against an edit that layered the option block without the two `dataset` fields. On a run that opted into 2 or 4, drop to the largest value in `[4, 2, 1]` that divides every selected camera width and height, apply it to all three fields, and fail before launch with the exact config patch if the selected recipe cannot express it. Print the resolved factor and selected camera resolutions in preflight output so reviewers can see the run's effective resolution.
- `harmonizer/3dgut: disabled`, `mesh: disabled` skip optional artifact-export pipelines that don't affect the trained Gaussians but add minutes per checkpoint. The reconstruction quality on the trained model is unchanged; only the exported artifacts are scoped down to checkpoint + parsed_config.
- `artifact: default` keeps the parsed config + checkpoint + rig_trajectories + sequence_tracks artifacts so the operator can inspect the run and re-launch with full artifacts later.

When extending `label_classes`: paste the full bundled default list verbatim from `configs/model/gaussians/composite/dynamic_gaussians.yaml`, then append the shard-specific class IDs the converter wrote. Cuboids whose `class_id` is not in any layer's `label_classes` are silently dropped; missing every class collapses dynamic-rigid reconstruction back to the static path, defeating [Select or create app config](#select-or-create-app-config)'s dynamic-config decision.

**Cross-check `label_classes`.** Cuboids whose `class_id` is not in any `label_classes` layer are silently dropped by NuRec. Inspect `configs/model/gaussians/composite/dynamic_gaussians.yaml` (or the fully-resolved `parsed.yaml`) -- if observed IDs are missing, either rename in the converter or extend the config via a custom mount during the NuRec launch.

**Check `track_label_sources`.** Some bundled configs restrict `dataset.cuboid_tracks_params.track_label_sources` (e.g. `- AUTOLABEL`), which drops observations whose shard-stored `LabelSource.name` is not in the list. Override the config (don't falsify converter provenance):

```yaml
# Hydra overrides at launch:
'dataset.cuboid_tracks_params.track_label_sources=null'          # accept any source
'dataset.cuboid_tracks_params.track_label_sources=[GT_ANNOTATION]'  # or pin the actual source
```

Inspect the resolved value with `grep -A5 track_label_sources <out_dir>/config/parsed.yaml`.

**Match sensor IDs (use ALL shard cameras; choose the single LiDAR deliberately).**
Bundled configs bake in a fixed `dataset.camera_ids` / `dataset.lidar_ids`
list -- any sensor not in that list is silently dropped from reconstruction,
even if it is present in the shard. **Always override both lists** explicitly.
Source of the override lists:

- **Operator-provided (preferred when present):** `nurec.camera_ids` and
  `nurec.lidar_ids` mirror the Hydra keys and are applied as
  `dataset.camera_ids` and `dataset.lidar_ids`. Require exactly one LiDAR ID for
  now; verify every listed id appears in the shard (`component_stores`) and fail
  fast otherwise.
- **Shard enumeration (default):** when the input does not specify a list,
  enumerate from the sequence meta JSON:

```python
import json
meta = json.load(open("<data.ncore_path>"))
stores = meta["component_stores"]
camera_ids = sorted(s.split("/")[-2] for s in stores if "/cameras/" in s)
lidar_ids_all = sorted(s.split("/")[-2] for s in stores if "/lidars/"  in s)
# -> produce Hydra overrides:
#    'dataset.camera_ids=[<cam0>,<cam1>,...]' 'dataset.lidar_ids=[<selected_lidar>]'
```

- **Cameras:** pass the full shard set (or the operator-provided subset).
  Omitting a camera discards the pixels it could contribute to the reconstruction.
- **LiDARs:** see [LiDAR selection for reconstruction](#lidar-selection-for-reconstruction) -- NuRec currently trains on
  a **single** LiDAR per run, so `dataset.lidar_ids` must contain exactly one entry
  regardless of how many LiDARs the shard holds.

Exceptions:

- Some training configs reserve specific cameras for validation; if the bundled config's `dataset.*_val_camera_ids` is populated, keep that partition but ensure every shard camera is listed in `camera_ids ∪ val_camera_ids` (no sensor silently omitted).
- Omit a camera only when the input explicitly excludes it, or the diagnosis specifically blames it (e.g. a broken intrinsic that would poison the whole run) -- and record the latter as a `nurec_config_issue` so the workflow surfaces the exclusion.

### LiDAR selection for reconstruction

NuRec currently asserts exactly **one**
LiDAR per training batch: when a batch would otherwise include more than one
LiDAR it raises `"multiple lidar sensors per batch is not supported for now"`.
A NuRec run therefore consumes a single LiDAR id regardless of how many LiDARs
the sequence contains, so `dataset.lidar_ids` must be a one-element list. (The
`sample_all_sensors: true` sampler default only works for single-LiDAR sequences;
combining it with multiple LiDARs trips the assert.)

**Operator override.** When the input provides `nurec.lidar_ids`, require
exactly one entry, use it directly as the selected LiDAR, verify it exists in
the shard, skip the policy below, and record `operator_override: true` in the
diagnosis `nurec_lidar_selection` entry with a rationale of "operator-specified
via input `nurec.lidar_ids`". Otherwise apply this policy:

1. **Prefer the longest-range, widest-FOV unit** -- typically a roof-mounted 360-deg
   spinning LiDAR. It alone usually covers the reconstruction volume, and is the unit
   that every bundled NuRec single-LiDAR sensor config selects.
2. **Exclude short-range side / corner units.** They are perception sensors rather than
   reconstruction sensors, and since NuRec consumes only one LiDAR per run they cannot
   contribute in parallel to the primary unit; NuRec's bundled configs never include them.
3. **If OOM persists with the selected LiDAR**, this is outside what `nurec-onboard`
   can fix automatically. Check NuRec's _Hardware Requirements_ (minimum 24 GB GPU
   memory, 48 GB recommended) and, if additional GPUs are available, NuRec's
   _Run on Multi-GPU Systems_ guide (`trainer.world_size` / `trainer.num_nodes`).
   Record the OOM as a `nurec_config_issue` for operator follow-up.

Record the decision under `nurec_lidar_selection` in the diagnosis (see
[Build diagnosis](#build-diagnosis)) with `{selected_id, excluded_ids, rationale, operator_override}` -- `selected_id`
is the single LiDAR passed via `dataset.lidar_ids`; `excluded_ids` is a flat list of LiDAR
id strings (every other shard LiDAR) -- per-unit reasons go in `rationale` as a single
narrative covering both the selection of `selected_id` and the exclusions; `operator_override`
is `true` when the id came from the input and `false` when it came from the policy.

**Authored-config artifact.** Write the custom config to `<nurec_output_dir>/custom_config.yaml`. Inspect bundled options directly in `<nurec_src>/configs/apps/`. Mount source, data, output, and any external component-store directories at their absolute host paths so metadata references remain valid.

### Run NuRec reconstruction

The auxiliary-data Docker flag rules apply here as well. NuRec Onboard always launches with the custom SQA-recipe config authored during config selection -- never points `--config-name` at a bundled `apps/AV/...` directly (bundled configs pin dataset-specific sensor IDs that mismatch the shard).

```bash
docker run --shm-size=64g --gpus all -d \
  --name nurec-<sequence_id>-<run_name> \
  --user <uid>:<gid> \
  -e HOME=<nurec_cache>/build-home -e USER=<username> \
  -e CCACHE_DIR=<nurec_cache>/ccache -e HF_TOKEN \
  <build_mounts> \
  -v <nurec_src>:<nurec_src>:ro \
  -v <workdir>:<workdir> \
  -v <data_dir>:<data_dir> \
  -v <nurec_output_dir>:<nurec_output_dir> \
  -w <nurec_src> \
  <dev_image> \
  bazelisk --output_base=<nurec_cache>/output_base --bazelrc=<nurec_cache>/nurec.bazelrc \
  run //:run -- \
  --config-name=<nurec_output_dir>/custom_config.yaml \
  out_dir=<nurec_output_dir> \
  mode=trainval \
  dataset.path=<data_dir>/<sequence_meta.json> \
  logger=dummy
```

The custom config bakes in `dataset.camera_ids` / `dataset.lidar_ids` during config selection, so **omit** those overrides on the command line -- repeating them risks the override and the YAML drifting. When `--config-name` is absolute, NuRec uses that file's parent as the config root while keeping the bundled `configs/` on Hydra's search path, so the SQA recipe's `defaults:` chain (`/apps/AV/_base_3dgut_dynamic.yaml`, `/apps/prod/options/...`) still resolves.

Pair the detached launch with the shared per-call polling pattern documented in [docker-execution.md "Long-running containers"](docker-execution.md#long-running-containers-detach-and-poll). Clean up the container with `docker rm <name>` once the diagnosis has consumed `docker logs` and the captured exit code.

**Common Hydra overrides:** `dataset.path` (container path to sequence JSON), `out_dir`, `mode=trainval|train|val|test`, `dataset.seek_offset_sec`, `dataset.duration_sec`, `logger=dummy|wandb|tensorboard`, `logger.offline=true`. Sensor IDs and the SQA option blocks live in the custom config, not on the command line.

**If training crashes (exit 255) on a LiDAR FOV-validity check** (the container log reports LiDAR beam directions / sensor angles falling outside the sensor's FOV): this crash should be caught pre-flight by the `check_lidar_model_fov_consistency` hard error (which instantiates the NCore model with `angles_to_columns_map_init=True` -- the same code path NuRec executes at training time). If it still occurs, it indicates validation was not run or the check was skipped. NuRec's LiDAR rasterizer enforces a per-(row, col) FOV check: stored ray directions must lie within the model's FOV defined by `(column_azimuths_rad[col] + row_azimuth_offsets_rad[row], row_elevations_rad[row])`. The exact log wording is not stable across NuRec versions, so match on the FOV / LiDAR-validity nature of the failure rather than a fixed string. Route as a `ncore_data_issue` back to `build-ncore-converter` (NOT a config issue):

- symptom: `"NuRec training crashes on a LiDAR FOV-validity check (stored beam directions fall outside the model's FOV)"`
- likely_cause: `"stored direction encodes per-ray geometry that the model parameters do not capture: either the sensor has non-zero per-beam azimuth offset \u0394 but row_azimuth_offsets_rad = 0 in the stored model (XYZ-derived direction includes \u0394, model FOV does not), or column_azimuths_rad is a rotor-phase-only schedule too coarse to host (rotor + \u0394)."`
- suggested_fix: `"Route to [build-ncore-converter/conventions.md row_azimuth_offsets_rad guidance](../build-ncore-converter/conventions.md#lidar-model-parameter-source-hierarchy). Pattern 1 (Sensor-native + Preserve) when the sensor publishes a \u0394 table and the rotor schedule is recoverable -- store real \u0394 in row_azimuth_offsets_rad and NN-bin the rotor-phase component into model_element[:, 1]. Pattern 3 (Synthetic-uniform + Encode-in-column) when the native rotor schedule cannot be cleanly recovered (rotor-phase-only streams, dual-return / near-field run patterns, or |\u0394| > native column step) -- synthesize a fine column_azimuths_rad (n_columns >= 3600 for 360-deg spinners), NN-bin per-ray (rotor + \u0394[ring]) against it, store row_azimuth_offsets_rad = 0. Both patterns make stored XYZ-derived directions FOV-valid by construction."`

### Interpret reconstruction output

The output directory contains `parsed.yaml` (fully-resolved Hydra config), checkpoints, validation renders, and -- when validation is enabled -- a `metrics.yaml` under `val/` with per-camera rendering quality KPIs (see NuRec `docs/public/nurec/model.rst`). Read the run-wide values from its `aggregated_metrics` mapping, whose keys are prefixed with the phase: `test/psnr`, `test/ssim`, and `test/lpips`. Record all three in the step summary under the unprefixed names.

For what each KPI measures, its scale/direction, and how to compare runs (no universal thresholds; regress against a known-good run at the same subsampling), see [diagnosis-reference.md "Rendering-quality metrics"](diagnosis-reference.md#rendering-quality-metrics).

### Build diagnosis

At completion, produce a structured diagnosis:

```yaml
reconstruction_status: success | issues_detected

# Read from metrics.yaml's aggregated_metrics under the phase-prefixed keys
# test/psnr, test/ssim, and test/lpips. A null blocks workflow_status: success.
metrics: { psnr: <float>, ssim: <float>, lpips: <float> }

subsampling:
  # The validator requires all three factors to match and divide every listed
  # selected camera dimension.
  camera_pixel_sampler_subsample: <int>
  n_val_image_subsample: <int>
  n_train_sequential_image_subsample: <int>
  selected_camera_resolutions:
    - camera_id: <cam0>
      width: <int>
      height: <int>

# Required whenever the shard has >= 1 LiDAR.
nurec_lidar_selection:
  # Single LiDAR id -- NuRec trains on one LiDAR per run. Passed via
  # dataset.lidar_ids=[<selected_id>].
  selected_id: <lidar0>
  # Flat list of LiDAR id strings (every other shard LiDAR). Per-unit reasons
  # go in `rationale`, not here.
  excluded_ids: [<lidar1>, ...]
  # Single narrative covering both the selection (why this unit: range / FOV /
  # coverage of reconstruction volume) and the exclusions (a one-clause
  # reason per excluded id). When `operator_override` is true, restate the
  # operator's reason.
  rationale: <string>
  # true when selected_id came from `nurec.lidar_ids`; false when it came from
  # the policy.
  operator_override: <bool>

# Both buckets carry severity: warning entries on a successful run. Only a
# severity: error entry is incompatible with reconstruction_status: success.
ncore_data_issues:
  - symptom: <string> # What was observed in reconstruction
    likely_cause: <string> # Mapped from the failure table below
    severity: error | warning

nurec_config_issues:
  - symptom: <string>
    likely_cause: <string>
    severity: error | warning
    # Actionable, machine-applicable fix -- the workflow's config-fix loop
    # uses this to re-launch run-nurec without rebuilding the converter.
    suggested_fix:
      kind: custom_config_edit | hydra_override
      # E.g. "swap inherited base to /apps/AV/_base_3dgut_dynamic.yaml",
      # "extend model.layers.dynamic_rigids.tracks.label_classes with
      # [car, truck]", or a Hydra override applied at the next launch.
      value: <string>
```

The two statuses partition on `severity`, not on whether an entry exists. `reconstruction_status: success` requires no `severity: error` entry in either bucket, and may carry `severity: warning` entries; `issues_detected` requires at least one `severity: error` entry. A finding that did not stop the reconstruction is a warning on an otherwise successful run. Reserve `severity: error` for findings that cost the run its result: an error entry routes the workflow into a fix loop and blocks `workflow_status: success`, so one marked `error` that the run survived spends an iteration and downgrades the verdict for nothing.
Before returning the diagnosis, write it to a temporary file and run:

```bash
cd "$NUREC_ONBOARD_DIR" && bazel run //skills/nurec-onboard/validators:run_nurec_validator -- <diagnosis.yaml>
```

A non-zero exit is a hard error; fix the diagnosis before returning it.

Map observed failures to causes and fixes using
[diagnosis-reference.md](diagnosis-reference.md): the
[NCore-related reconstruction failure mapping](diagnosis-reference.md#ncore-related-reconstruction-failure-mapping)
populates `ncore_data_issues`, the
[NuRec config-selection failure mapping](diagnosis-reference.md#nurec-config-selection-failure-mapping)
populates `nurec_config_issues` (each row carries the `suggested_fix.kind` / `value`
the config-fix loop applies), and the
[label_classes extension template](diagnosis-reference.md#label_classes-extension-template)
covers the "Cuboids ignored by training" fix. Check a log warning against
[Container warnings](diagnosis-reference.md#container-warnings) before mapping it
into either bucket: three of the messages the images emit describe their own
trigger inaccurately and appear in the logs of runs that completed.

> **Step attempt exit anchor:** capture `runs[*].ended_at` here, after [`validators/run_nurec_validator.py`](../../../validators/run_nurec_validator.py) returns. Compute `duration_sec`. Config-fix retries are _separate_ run-nurec invocations -- each gets its own `runs[*]` entry; the timer does not span across them.

---

## 3. Output

Return the structured diagnosis. This is consumed by:

- **nurec-onboard**: routes `ncore_data_issues` to `build-ncore-converter` (fix mode); feeds `nurec_config_issues[].suggested_fix` into its config-fix loop, which re-invokes `run-nurec` after applying the fix (no converter rebuild).
- If `reconstruction_status` is `success`, the workflow is complete.

---

## 4. Authoritative NuRec References

Do not duplicate NuRec config content. Inspect these files in the enclosing NuRec checkout:

- `configs/apps/` -- app configs
- `configs/dataset/ncore.yaml` -- dataset config schema
- `README.md` -- Hydra override syntax and config options

## 5. Constraints

- This step operates on NuRec containers only. Converter fixes route through `build-ncore-converter`.
- No user interaction -- pick a config autonomously; create a custom one if no bundled match.
